integrations.description: Connect accounts from other services. Google Drive and OneDrive become volumes you browse, copy to and sync with; Google Photos receives uploads and lets you import the photos you pick.

catalog.title: Connect a service
catalog.description: Pick the service and how it connects. "Account" means you only sign in. Google Cloud and Microsoft Entra mean you register your own client first: more control, more steps.

app.summary: Sign in with your Google account. Nothing to set up.
app.intro: WingDrive signs in with its own OAuth client, which is included in official builds. You only choose your account and allow access.
pros: No Google Cloud project: sign in and you are done.
Works the same on every device that runs an official WingDrive build.
Tokens stay encrypted in this library. No WingDrive server sees your files.
cons: Depends on the client included in the build; builds from source may not have one.
Until Google verifies the WingDrive app, Google shows an "unverified app" warning and caps how many people can sign in.
API quotas are shared by everyone who uses WingDrive's client.
steps: Choose Google Drive, Google Photos or both below.
Click Sign in with Google. Your browser opens Google's sign-in page.
Pick your account and allow the access WingDrive asks for.
Go back to WingDrive. Drive appears in the sidebar; repeat to add more accounts.
app.unavailable: This build does not include WingDrive's Google client. Use an official build, or connect with Google Cloud and your own client.

custom.summary: Use an OAuth client from your own Google Cloud project.
custom.intro: You create a "Desktop app" OAuth client in your own Google Cloud project and WingDrive signs in with it. Nothing depends on WingDrive's client.
pros: The project and its API quotas are yours alone.
Works in any build, including builds from source.
You decide which APIs and accounts have access, and can revoke everything in your project.
cons: Takes about ten minutes in Google Cloud Console.
While the consent screen is in testing mode, Google ends access every 7 days. Publish it to avoid that, even without verification.
The client is saved in this library only; other libraries need it saved again.
steps: Open console.cloud.google.com and create a project.
In APIs & Services > Library, enable Google Drive API, Photos Library API and Photos Picker API.
In OAuth consent screen, choose External, fill in the app name and add your Google accounts as test users.
In Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type Desktop app.
Paste the client ID and client secret below and save.
Click Sign in with Google Cloud.

app.summary: Sign in with a personal, work or school Microsoft account.
app.intro: WingDrive signs in with its own Microsoft app registration, which is included in official builds. You only choose your account and allow access.
pros: No Azure or Entra setup: sign in and you are done.
Works with personal accounts (Outlook, Hotmail) and with work or school accounts.
Tokens stay encrypted in this library. No WingDrive server sees your files.
cons: Depends on the app registration included in the build; builds from source may not have one.
Some organizations only allow apps an administrator approved.
Microsoft has no way for an app to revoke itself: after disconnecting, remove WingDrive at account.live.com/consent/Manage.
steps: Click Sign in with Microsoft. Your browser opens Microsoft's sign-in page.
Pick your account and accept the permissions WingDrive asks for.
Go back to WingDrive. OneDrive appears in the sidebar; repeat to add more accounts.
app.unavailable: This build does not include WingDrive's Microsoft app. Use an official build, or connect with Microsoft Entra and your own app.

custom.summary: Use an app you register in Microsoft Entra.
custom.intro: You register a public client app in Microsoft Entra and WingDrive signs in with its application (client) ID. Public clients use PKCE, so there is no secret to copy.
pros: The app registration is yours, in your own account or tenant.
No client secret to create, store or renew.
Fits organizations that only allow apps they registered themselves.
cons: Needs a free Azure account to reach Microsoft Entra.
Work or school tenants may need an administrator to consent to the app.
The app is saved in this library only; other libraries need it saved again.
steps: Open entra.microsoft.com and go to App registrations > New registration.
Under Supported account types, choose accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts.
Under Redirect URI, choose Public client/native (mobile & desktop) and enter http://localhost/oauth/callback.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the app's Overview page, paste it below and save.
Click Sign in with Microsoft Entra.
